2890: Prof. Dinesh Kumar delivered an engaging address that underscored the deep cultural ties between India and Japan, and emphasized the complementarity of the two nations in the economic as well as social development spheres. Highlighting the role collaboration can play in the progress of any nation, Prof. Dinesh Kumar hailed MIJSC for playing a crucial part in strengthening Indo-Japan bilateral ties through academic research, executive education as well as cultural exchange. “During the same celebrations next year, I am sure we will have more projects and collaborative initiatives to boast of.”
2891: Prof. Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIM Bangalore, said, “This is a historic gift to IIM Bangalore and to the cause of institution-building. The School of Undergraduate Studies is being conceived at a time when AI is reshaping the way businesses, governments and society operate. Through world-class infrastructure, research capability and globally benchmarked learning, IIM Bangalore aims to nurture an ecosystem where students deeply engage with the defining challenges of an AI-driven world”.
2892: Prof. Gopal Naik in his closing remarks said that the CPP conference on public policy and management is aimed to support PhD students to pursue research on public policy and present their research, as well as to motivate them to do more rigorous work on public policy and make the same available to practitioners. “This interaction between researchers and practitioners will be the key to identification of more areas for research. Practitioners will also get to know the results of studies already conducted.”
2893: Prof. Gopal Naik, Chairperson, Senior Fellow and Jal Jeevan Mission Chair Professor at the Centre for Public Policy, IIM Bangalore, said: “IIM Bangalore is glad to host the launch of this case study. Delivering water at scale is one challenge, and sustaining it is another. This study brings together twenty-five years of experience from Gujarat and India to show what works and what comes next. Its lessons on governance, community ownership and ambition are practical ones. Building water systems is one task; sustaining them is another. Twenty-five years of evidence lets us ask what lasted, and why.”
2894: Prof. Haritha Saranga, Chairperson, IIMB Sustainability Taskforce, thanked all staff members for their continued commitment to the Institute's sustainability journey, noting that this recognition reflects the collective effort of everyone who works, day in and day out, to build a greener campus.
2895: Prof. M. S. Narasimhan, Academic Director, IIMBx Digital Learning Foundation, pointed out that Fintech professionals have the potential to create abundant employment opportunities as they create their businesses. “The course will help you create more products as well as ventures and spot gaps. Be an ambassador of the programme for future batches, retain your learning habit and help enhance the state's reputation as a FinTech powerhouse.”

2898: Prof. Tatsuya Terazawa discussed the complex issue of the Energy Trilemma plaguing the world today. “It is very challenging to achieve the objectives of energy security, energy equity and environmental sustainability, simultaneously”, he lamented. He spoke about issues arising out of the current geopolitical situation, wars, sanctions, etc. and added that there existed a conflict between energy security and energy affordability.
2899: Prof. U Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIM Bangalore, delivered the inaugural address, congratulating the incoming cohort and emphasising the importance of artificial intelligence in transforming governance and public service delivery, from healthcare access through frontline workers to reducing the cost of public services, while cautioning that its adoption must be balanced against its impact on employment.
2900: Prof. U Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIMB, said, “The value of research is strengthened when it engages with the problems businesses face and subsequently informs decision-making. At IIMB, we see cases as an important way of making that connection by bringing research, managerial experience and real business problems into the classroom. The global adoption of our cases shows that there is demand for teaching material that is rigorous, contemporary and grounded in the realities of business”.
2901: Prof. U. Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIM Bangalore, opened his address by thanking the many people and institutions behind the school's creation, including the Government of Karnataka for granting more than 100 acres of land for the upcoming campus, Dr. Shetty and the Board of Governors, former IIM Bangalore directors Prof. Raghuram Rajan and Prof. Rishikesha T Krishnan, along with Prof. Nayana Tara, former faculty, IIMB, with the Tata Trusts, and partners including Axis Bank, State Street and Wipro. 2902: Prof. U. Dinesh Kumar, Director-in-charge, IIMB, delivered the opening address with a call for scrutiny of AI's promise versus its reality, noting that AI systems are fundamentally probabilistic and inherit the strengths and weaknesses of the data beneath them, citing the Dutch childcare benefits scandal as a reminder of how flawed data can produce serious social consequences.

2906: Professor Das’s scholarship has a strong international orientation. She has been a Research Fellow at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies, Geneva, and has been associated with the Exeter Centre for Environmental Law, contributing to interdisciplinary research on environmental regulation and sustainability transitions. She has also received competitive research funding from the Zurich University of Applied Sciences, supporting collaborative work on local environmental democracy and green transitions. In addition to her research and teaching, Professor Das is actively involved in the design of international immersion initiatives at IIM Bangalore. She designed and led the inaugural Business Planning for International Markets (BPIM) programme’s Switzerland module, marking IIMB’s first engagement with the Swiss market. The course examines how firms navigate international markets shaped by strong regulatory regimes, sustainability imperatives, and complex institutional contexts. The module included academic and practitioner engagements with key international institutions such as the World Health Organization, the United Nations Office at Geneva, Deloitte, the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies, the University of Geneva, the Geneva Chancellery, and the Swiss-Indian Chamber of Commerce, offering participants a first-hand understanding of the institutional architecture shaping global business and policy environments. At IIM Bangalore, Professor Das teaches environmental politics at the doctoral level and the core Business, Government, and Society: Ethics and Responsible Business course for PGP students. Across her teaching, research, and programme engagement, she consistently emphasises the importance of understanding markets as institutionally embedded systems shaped by regulation, social norms, and public purpose.
